hypotheses.reasoning: Checkout was healthy until 08:31:27, when requests were still returning 200 in about 200ms. At 08:31:45 the external card processor (api.cardproc.example) started answering payment-svc with 502/503. payment-svc's circuit breaker opened at 08:33:15 with a 92% failure rate. Its half-open probes at 08:36:24 and 08:41:27 also got 502/503, so the provider was still down. Because the breaker was open, payment-svc returned 503 to order-service, and the gateway then returned 503 on POST /checkout. Nothing in the logs points to an internal cause: there are no deploy lines, redis and postgres look normal, and the slow audit_log query (08:26) and gateway disk warning (08:25) came before the onset and have nothing to do with checkout.
Some gateway 503s took 10-29s, which could mean upstream latency. But the provider answered with explicit 5xx codes rather than timing out.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the card processor (api.cardproc.example) outage on its status page or with its support team. If you have a backup payment processor, switch to it, or queue checkout charges and retry them later. Show users a clear "payment temporarily unavailable" message. Shorten order-service and gateway timeouts so that failing fast while the circuit is open doesn't tie up connections for 10-29s.
